why_this_persona: A library of ten thousand ready-made templates is the exact trap Emma is already in: her own file lists a Zapier or Make trial with a few half-built flows, more apps than she uses, and a backlog of ideas at night. She is also the only one of the three who opens a builder canvas at all; Rick will not build a stack and Anna uses what the company already pays for.
interest: Automating my process: Prioritising the 1,000 automation ideas: which two are worth it
question: I have a hundred ideas and a few half-finished ones. Which two are actually worth building this month?

borrow.hook_logic: A found object with a number on it. The source says what it found and how much of it there is and lets the count carry the hook instead of an adjective ('10 Thousand plus Automation templates'). Ours opens on the same library and the same count, then turns it into a decision. I-13 is the reason the number stays: naming specific things is the only language feature that predicts reach and survives creator normalisation.
borrow.proof_mechanism: The screen is the proof. Scroll the thing on camera rather than describe it: I-08 makes putting a screen on camera the most reliable visual finding in the corpus, I-09 puts the first frame on the screen rather than the face. Ours adds a second screen the source does not have, our own canvas with the unfinished ones still on it.
borrow.ordering: The find, what is inside it, what you do with it. We keep the first two and replace the third: the three questions, and what is left standing after them.
borrow.visual_grammar: Full screen capture with no face at the open, the count visible, one subject held rather than cut around. Inferred from the caption, the duration and the format only: no frame analysis exists for this code.

change.process: Choosing which repeating chore in a 1 to 8 person online business gets built this month: the same twenty customer questions, the where-is-my-order replies, the ad numbers she needs every morning on one screen, or the product copy done in batches instead of one item at a time.
change.friction: A library answers what could be built and never what should exist here. Emma already pays for more apps than she uses and already has half-built flows on the canvas from a trial, so a ten-thousand-and-first template does not fix any of them. The chore that is worth it is the one with an owner, a number it is supposed to move, and a home inside work she already does.
change.ai_boundary: The machine copies the steps in minutes and can fill a canvas faster than she can name what it is for. A person picks the chore, names the number it has to move, and decides where it lives. Anything that reaches a customer, a reply or a returns decision, waits in a draft queue for her approval before it sends.
change.next_action: Comment AUDIT, run the three questions across the flows already on your canvas this week, and kill the ones that fail all three before building anything new.

hook: Ten thousand ready-made templates online. Three questions pick the two chores worth handing over this month, and kill the rest.

on_screen.opening_screen: The template library itself, scrolling, count visible on screen, no face. Then our own canvas next to it, with the half-built ones still sitting there, badly named.
on_screen.human_check: Each surviving chore gets an owner's name and a review date written on the flow itself. The one that touches a customer reply runs as a draft queue Emma approves, plus a weekly look at a sample of what it actually sent.
on_screen.cost_line: Emma already pays $20 to $100 a month across several tools, and $20 is this audience's reference price. The number that decides is that bill divided by how often the job actually runs: a flow that fires twice a month costs more per run than doing it by hand, and that is the month it stops paying.

cta.viewer_gets: One page with three questions: who owns it, what number it is supposed to move, and where it lives inside work you already do. Run it on what you have before you build another one.

notes: This is a free-resource post, the category I-25 puts on M2's refusal list, and a tool list is a named Radar disqualifier in RULES.md §2. It is taken only because the card is the decision rather than the library: Radar needs a concrete task, a decision and a limitation, and the limitation is that a template carries somebody else's exceptions, never this shop's. The routing hint scored Emma 0.59 on the single word 'website', which is noise; the match is the interest line about prioritising the ideas, not the word. The source has no comment keyword in its caption and still earned 35.7 shares per thousand; ours adds one because a real sheet exists for this interest (RULES.md §12.3). n8n itself is named late and only as the place the templates live, per rule 13a.
